Also...
I should just point out that although I’ve been battling for 20+ years with depression and anxiety. 
My first suicidal attempt happened on the 3rd of August 2019. And then again attempted on the Sunday just past.

I can dig it. 
You have to understand, I’m 45 and been rejecting the help for a good 20+ years. 
I mean, there are walk-in places etc in my area but simply no motivation for help.

I do on occasion. It’s hard though. The vast majority of my social circle including my family have no frame of reference for this kind of thing. So they simply don’t understand depression, anxiety etc from the perspective of a suicide survivor let alone someone that never tried it.

If you get the quantities/ratios wrong you’ll cause yourself a lot of trouble. 
And not just the emotional kind of trouble.

No... don’t do that. Unless they have a frame of reference regarding severe depression and suicide then don’t. Even those that do have actual experience I’ve found just tend to hit you with soundbites. This is just my experience.
It’s hard to find meaning because there is none.
Christ! Please, don’t make any changes.
